description: Shadow catalogue of keystone technology candidates. A row with status 'confirmed' MUST have a fully encoded entry at data/<domain>/ carrying the same id — H001 checks this both ways, after run-001-baseline found the Great Law of Peace filed under two different ids. A row with status 'shadow' is a candidate nobody has encoded yet; it is a research target, not a claim.

entries.name: Terra Preta (Amazonian Dark Earth)
entries.description: Engineered biochar-rich soils combining charcoal, organics, and pottery shards for long-lived fertility and carbon sequestration.

entries.name: Andean Terraces
entries.description: Slope stabilization and microclimate agriculture on mountain terrain.

entries.name: Australian Firestick Farming
entries.description: Biodiversity management via controlled burns; landscape-scale ecological engineering.

entries.name: Nile Flood Basin Agriculture
entries.description: Natural silt fertilization cycles harnessing annual flood patterns.

entries.name: Chinampas
entries.description: Floating gardens; high-yield wetland agriculture on lake beds.

entries.name: Ifugao Rice Terraces
entries.description: Communal management of mountainous rice systems; living cultural landscape.

entries.name: Agroforestry in West Africa
entries.description: Integrating crops with nitrogen-fixing trees (e.g., Faidherbia) for soil renewal.

entries.name: Wampum Belts
entries.description: Treaty and value exchange encoded in mnemonic shell bead form.

entries.name: Potlatch
entries.description: Redistributive wealth regulation through ceremonial giving.

entries.name: Cowrie Shell Currency
entries.description: Durable, portable, hard-to-counterfeit natural currency spanning continents.

entries.name: Silk Road Trade Network
entries.description: Distributed, redundant transcontinental supply chain for goods and knowledge.

entries.name: Salt Trade
entries.description: Critical preservation commodity forming the basis of wealth and exchange routes.

entries.name: Maya Cacao Currency
entries.description: Dual role as ritual medium and trade currency; biodegradable wealth.

entries.name: Roman Coinage Standardization
entries.description: Early centralized minting for wide empire economic cohesion.

entries.name: Great Law of Peace (Haudenosaunee)
entries.description: Distributed councils with women's veto; federated governance model.

entries.name: Athenian Sortition
entries.description: Randomized citizen governance; lottery-based democracy.

entries.name: Ubuntu
entries.description: Relational ethics: 'I am because we are.' Communal personhood philosophy.

entries.name: Indus Valley Sanitation Committees
entries.description: Decentralized civic planning for public sanitation infrastructure.

entries.name: Songhai Bureaucracy
entries.description: Early centralized recordkeeping for empire-scale administration.

entries.name: Icelandic Althing
entries.description: One of the world's oldest parliaments; consensus-based lawmaking.

entries.name: Polynesian Chiefly Councils
entries.description: Distributed navigation and resource decisions across islands.

entries.name: Quipu (Khipu)
entries.description: Knotted-cord information system for census, accounts, and narratives; low-infrastructure data tech.

entries.name: Songlines
entries.description: Oral-mnemonic geospatial maps encoding navigation, law, and ecology in song.

entries.name: Printing Press
entries.description: Scalable replication of text; democratized knowledge distribution.

entries.name: Arabic Numerals
entries.description: Positional decimal system enabling advanced mathematics and commerce.

entries.name: Maya Long Count Calendar
entries.description: Precise astronomical tracking with cycles spanning millennia.

entries.name: House of Wisdom (Baghdad)
entries.description: Translation and preservation hub; cross-cultural scholarly synthesis.

entries.name: Oracle Bone Script
entries.description: Earliest durable logographic writing; divination records on bone and shell.

entries.name: Library of Alexandria
entries.description: Cataloging and scholarly correspondence as infrastructure; knowledge nexus.

entries.name: Precision Lathe
entries.description: Mother of machine tools; enabled precision manufacturing at scale.

entries.name: Arch and Dome
entries.description: Enduring architecture distributing force through curvature.

entries.name: Compass
entries.description: Magnetic navigation enabling oceanic exploration and trade.

entries.name: Gunpowder
entries.description: Chemistry-driven military and mining applications; transformative energetics.

entries.name: Stirrups
entries.description: Revolutionized mounted mobility and cavalry warfare.

entries.name: Damascus Steel
entries.description: Metallurgical innovation combining strength and flexibility; nanotube patterns.

entries.name: Benin Bronze Casting
entries.description: Lost-wax precision casting unmatched for centuries; art and engineering fused.

entries.name: Paper
entries.description: Scalable medium for knowledge storage and spread.

entries.name: Windmills
entries.description: First industrial-scale harnessing of wind for grinding and pumping.

entries.name: Women's War Councils
entries.description: Women's veto power on violence; gendered checks on aggression.

entries.name: Resource Taboos
entries.description: Ecological law embedded in culture; sacred limits on resource extraction.

entries.name: Hospitality Codes
entries.description: Safety through reciprocity; sacred obligation to shelter strangers.

entries.name: Restorative Justice Circles
entries.description: Reintegration over exclusion; community-centered conflict resolution.

entries.name: Bushido
entries.description: Codified ethics of honor and duty, balancing violence with restraint.

entries.name: Monastic Rule of St. Benedict
entries.description: Regulated labor, prayer, and education in communities; blueprint for institutional life.

entries.name: Ashoka's Edicts
entries.description: Stone-carved ethical governance: animal welfare, tolerance, non-violence at state scale.

entries.name: Indus Valley Plumbing
entries.description: Decentralized drains and sewers; earliest urban sanitation at scale.

entries.name: Roman Aqueducts
entries.description: Centralized but high-reliability gravity-fed water supply over vast distances.

entries.name: Polynesian Fishponds
entries.description: Sustainable aquaculture infrastructure; managed coastal ecosystems.

entries.name: Great Zimbabwe Walls
entries.description: Dry-stone engineering without mortar; monumental precision construction.

entries.name: Qanat Irrigation
entries.description: Underground channels tapping groundwater; gravity-driven desert irrigation.

entries.name: Stepwells
entries.description: Civic water management combined with community gathering spaces.

entries.name: Medieval Cathedral Networks
entries.description: Knowledge transmission through stonemasonry guilds; distributed building schools.

entries.name: Inca Road System
entries.description: 40,000 km of paths and rope bridges knitting empire without wheels.

entries.name: Budj Bim Eel Aquaculture (Gunditjmara)
entries.description: Stone channels, weirs, and holding ponds cut into a lava flow to farm short-finned eels; hydraulic infrastructure built without agriculture.
entries.source_note: Channels radiocarbon-dated to at least c. 6600 cal BP (McNiven et al. 2012); UNESCO World Heritage 2019.

entries.name: Kula Ring (Massim ceremonial exchange)
entries.description: Inter-island circuit in which two classes of never-consumed valuable move in fixed opposite directions, carrying trust and ordinary trade with them.
entries.source_note: Malinowski (1922); substantially revised by Leach & Leach (1983).

entries.name: Nunuku-whenua's Covenant (Moriori)
entries.description: Absolute proscription on killing enforced as law for roughly three centuries, with bounded staff combat substituted for lethal violence.
entries.source_note: Moriori oral tradition; King (1989); 1870 Native Land Court testimony; absence of pā-type fortification.

entries.name: Hxaro (Ju/'hoansi delayed reciprocal exchange)
entries.description: Named lifelong partnerships with deliberately delayed, non-equivalent return, maintaining callable claims on distant groups' resources.
entries.source_note: Wiessner (1982, 2002). Encoded deliberately failing the rubric — see data/social/hxaro.json.

entries.name: Gadaa System
entries.description: Generational grade system rotating political, ritual, and military authority on a fixed eight-year cycle with mandatory handover.
entries.source_note: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2016. Notable as term limits enforced by cosmology rather than by constitution.

entries.name: Xeer (Somali customary law)
entries.description: Polycentric customary law of compensation and elder arbitration, contracted between lineage groups and operating without a state.
entries.source_note: Continued to function through the post-1991 collapse of central government — a rare natural experiment in law without a state.

entries.name: Subak Water Temple Networks
entries.description: Irrigation coordinated through a hierarchy of water temples whose ritual calendar sets planting schedules across a whole watershed.
entries.source_note: UNESCO 2012. Lansing's modelling showed the temple schedule approximates the optimum trade-off between water sharing and pest control — the Green Revolution's attempt to override it reduced yields.

entries.name: Acequia Ditch Commons
entries.region: Iberia and the Rio Grande basin
entries.description: Gravity irrigation ditches governed as a commons by shared labour obligation under an elected mayordomo.
entries.source_note: Andalusi origin, transmitted via New Spain; still legally recognised as political subdivisions in New Mexico.

entries.name: Waru Waru Raised Fields
entries.description: Raised planting platforms separated by water channels whose stored daytime heat buffers night frost at 3800m.
entries.source_note: Abandoned pre-conquest; experimentally rebuilt from the 1980s with measured frost protection and yield gains.

entries.name: Nabataean Runoff Farming
entries.description: Micro-catchment terraces and conduits concentrating scarce runoff onto small plots in under 100mm annual rainfall.
entries.source_note: Reconstructed and operated experimentally at Avdat and Shivta through the 20th century.

entries.name: Yakhchāl Ice Storage
entries.description: Conical mudbrick chambers using radiative night cooling, evaporative shading, and subterranean mass to hold ice through desert summers.
entries.source_note: Paired with qanats and windcatchers; a working passive refrigeration system with no energy input.

entries.name: Marshallese Stick Charts
entries.description: Lattice charts encoding ocean swell refraction and interference around islands — a map of wave behaviour, not of coastline.
entries.source_note: Mattang, meddo, and rebbelib classes. Memorised on land and not carried aboard: the artefact is a teaching device for a body skill.

entries.name: Polynesian Non-Instrument Wayfinding
entries.description: Deep-ocean navigation by star houses, swell, cloud, and bird behaviour, holding a dead-reckoned position across weeks without instruments.
entries.source_note: Near-extinguished, then transmitted from Mau Piailug (Satawal) to the Polynesian Voyaging Society; demonstrated by Hōkūle'a from 1976.

entries.name: Talking Drums (surrogate speech)
entries.description: Tonal languages transposed onto drum pitch, transmitting arbitrary sentences over distance with stock phrases supplying redundancy.
entries.source_note: A speech-surrogate channel with built-in error correction, roughly a millennium before information theory named the problem.

entries.name: Winter Counts (waníyetu wowápi)
entries.description: Pictographic chronologies on hide, one image per year, maintained by a designated keeper as a shared index for oral history.
entries.source_note: Independent counts can be cross-checked against each other and against dated events such as the 1833 Leonid meteor storm.

entries.name: Göbekli Tepe and the Taş Tepeler enclosures
entries.description: Monumental carved-pillar enclosures raised by populations without agriculture, domesticated animals, or pottery.
entries.source_note: Direct counter-evidence to surplus-first models of monumental construction. Karahan Tepe and related sites show it was not a one-off, and 2025 excavation there reported a c. 17m tiered enclosure with stone benches and carved heads set into the walls — seating, at a site with no agriculture.

entries.name: Upano Valley Urbanism
entries.description: Thousands of earthen platforms linked by wide sunken roads across the Amazonian foothills, revealed by airborne LIDAR.
entries.source_note: Rostain et al. (2024), Science. A major recent revision to how densely the pre-Columbian Amazon was settled.

entries.name: Cahokia
entries.description: Planned mound city with an engineered central plaza and solar calendar posts; the largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico.
entries.source_note: Rapid coalescence around 1050 and near-complete depopulation by 1350 — as much a case study in collapse as in construction.

entries.name: Nan Madol
entries.description: Ceremonial complex of roughly a hundred artificial islets built from columnar basalt logs laid in a lagoon.
entries.source_note: The transport method for basalt columns weighing several tonnes each remains unresolved.

entries.name: Hohokam Canal Network
entries.description: Several hundred kilometres of hand-dug gravity canals irrigating the Salt and Gila valleys without draft animals or metal tools.
entries.source_note: Modern Phoenix canals follow Hohokam alignments — the survey work was good enough to reuse.

entries.name: Baiame's Ngunnhu (Brewarrina fish traps)
entries.description: Stone weirs and holding pens across half a kilometre of river, worked cooperatively by several nations under agreed protocol.
entries.source_note: Candidate independent replication for budj_bim; the two systems would settle the replication_regions question for Aboriginal aquaculture.

entries.name: Chuño Freeze-Drying
entries.description: Alternating night frost, day sun, and treading to dehydrate potatoes into a form storable for years and detoxified of glycoalkaloids.
entries.source_note: Underwrote Andean state granaries; the technology is a climate exploit, requiring the altiplano's specific diurnal swing.

entries.name: Meroitic Iron Production
entries.description: Large-scale bloomery smelting with slag heaps still standing metres high around the royal city.
entries.source_note: Long read through a colonial frame as derivative of Egypt or Assyria; the metallurgical evidence does not require that reading.

entries.name: Kayak (qajaq)
entries.description: Skin-on-frame hull built to its individual paddler's body dimensions, with a recovery roll making capsize survivable in lethal water.
entries.source_note: Bespoke fit as a design principle — the anthropometric standard is one person, not a population mean.

entries.name: Hima Rangeland Reserves
entries.description: Grazing reserves closed or rotated under customary and religious authority, with community enforcement of the closure.
entries.source_note: One of the longest continuously documented commons regimes; heavily eroded during 20th-century land nationalisations, with partial revival since.

entries.name: Gacaca Community Courts
entries.description: Customary dispute-resolution form scaled up by statute to process roughly 1.9 million genocide cases before elected lay judges.
entries.source_note: Included precisely because its record is contested — throughput and participation were extraordinary, and documented failures of due process and witness protection are serious. A codex that only encodes successes is a brochure.

entries.name: Age-Set Systems
entries.description: Cohorts initiated together and moving through graded roles for life, creating bonds that deliberately cut across lineage and locality.
entries.source_note: Structurally a redundancy mechanism: loyalties that cross descent lines make lineage feud harder to sustain.

entries.name: Sande and Poro Societies
entries.description: Parallel women's and men's initiation societies holding regulatory authority over knowledge, conduct, and dispute across ethnic boundaries.
entries.source_note: Authority spanning several language groups; among the few widely documented cases of parallel gendered institutions with genuinely separate jurisdictions.

entries.name: Crooked Tree Wetland Fisheries
entries.description: Canals steering seasonal floodwater into holding ponds to concentrate fish, built by Late Archaic foragers before maize agriculture.
entries.source_note: Harrison-Buck et al. (2024), Science Advances 10(47), doi:10.1126/sciadv.adq1444.

entries.name: Lake Tesse Trout Translocation
entries.description: Brown trout carried above impassable barriers into barren mountain lakes and harvested with wooden traps; earliest documented human translocation of a fish species.
entries.source_note: Mjærum et al. (2026), Antiquity, doi:10.15184/aqy.2026.10392.

entries.name: Monte Sierpe (Band of Holes)
entries.description: About 5,200 aligned pits running 1.5km along a mountainside, segmented in a pattern mirroring khipu structure — a barter marketplace under the Chincha, an accounting register under the Inca.
entries.source_note: Bongers et al. (2025), Antiquity, doi:10.15184/aqy.2025.10237. Drone survey plus microbotanical sampling of 19 pits found maize and basketry reeds; colonial-era citrus pollen shows use continued after 1532. Files under information rather than economic because the keystone claim is a record-keeping system inscribed into terrain — a sibling to quipu, which is already encoded and whose structure it echoes.

entries.name: Eridu Irrigation Network
entries.description: Over 200 major canals and some 4,000 minor channels feeding roughly 700 farms, preserved intact because the Euphrates shifted course and left the whole system stranded.
entries.source_note: Jotheri et al. (2025), Antiquity, doi:10.15184/aqy.2025.19. Rare because abandonment preserved the full network rather than the usual palimpsest of recut channels — one of the few places the whole topology of an ancient irrigation system can be read at once.

entries.name: Tehuacán Valley Travertine Canals
entries.description: Roughly 400km of spring-fed canals whose walls self-seal with precipitated travertine, plus the Purrón Dam; parts still carry water.
entries.source_note: Neely, Aiuvalasit & Winsborough (2022), The Holocene; Purrón Dam redated by OSL and AMS. Candidate for the longest continuously used water management system in the Americas — the self-sealing travertine lining is the unusual engineering property and is worth checking before encoding.

entries.name: Didé West Iron Smelting Workshop
entries.description: Well-preserved iron-smelting workshop in West Africa, adding direct process evidence to a metallurgical tradition long read through a diffusionist frame.
entries.source_note: Reported 2026. Pairs with the meroe_iron candidate; together they test whether sub-Saharan ironworking needs an external origin story at all.

entries.name: Andean Chocó Forest Earthworks
entries.description: Human landscape modification found under closed tropical canopy by LIDAR, in a region previously mapped as essentially unoccupied.
entries.source_note: Reported 2026; extent and dating not yet well characterised, which is why this is a research target and not a claim. Listed because it is the same failure mode as Upano: 'no sites here' meaning 'nobody has flown a laser over it'.
